preauthor_statement: Let $p>0$ and let $\mu$ be a $p$-restricted partition ([[def-p-regular-and-p-restricted-partitions]]). A node $(r,c)$ is an $i$-node if its residue $\operatorname{res}(r,c):=c-r\bmod p$ equals $i\in\mathbb Z/p$; the $i$-nodes of $\mu$ are its addable and removable nodes of residue $i$ ([[def-removable-and-addable-nodes-of-a-partition]]). Fix $i$ and list the $i$-nodes $A_1,\dots,A_n$ from top to bottom (increasing row index, then increasing column index). Form the word $\sigma=(\sigma_1,\dots,\sigma_n)$ with $\sigma_m=+$ if $A_m$ is addable and $\sigma_m=-$ if $A_m$ is removable. Whenever $r<s$, $\sigma_r=-$, $\sigma_s=+$ and $\sigma_{r+1}=\dots=\sigma_{s-1}=0$, replace $\sigma_r,\sigma_s$ by $0$; repeat until no $-$ lies to the left of a $+$. The resulting reduced $i$-signature has the form $+\cdots+-\cdots-$ with the zeros deleted: the removable nodes corresponding to its $-$ signs are the normal $i$-nodes, the topmost (first listed) of these is the good $i$-node, the addable nodes corresponding to its $+$ signs are the conormal $i$-nodes, the bottommost (last listed) of these is the cogood $i$-node. Write $\varepsilon_i(\mu)$ and $\varphi_i(\mu)$ for the numbers of normal and of conormal $i$-nodes. The residue $c-r$ is the negative of Brundan's $\ell$-residue $r-c$, and a removable node is normal here exactly when its transposed node is normal in Brundan's sense for the transpose partition; the two conventions must never be mixed silently. At most one cogood node and at most one good node occur in each residue.
